typeName: Q3: Inference (a test or an interval)
title: Exercise and sleep quality: a chi-square test for independence

stimulus.title: Exercise and sleep quality
stimulus.html:
A health agency selects a random sample of 500 adults in a large state. Each adult reports how many days a week they exercise for at least 30 minutes and rates their usual sleep quality. The agency wants to know whether exercise and sleep quality are associated for adults in the state. (Invented data.)
Observed counts: days of exercise per week by sleep quality
ExercisePoor sleepFair sleepGood sleepTotal
None525840150
1 to 2 days457065180
3 or more days306278170
Total127190183500

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the null and alternative hypotheses for a test of whether exercise and sleep quality are associated.

rubric.point: Correct hypotheses in context: H_0: there is no association between days of exercise and sleep quality for adults in the state; H_a: there is an association.
accept: H_0: exercise and sleep quality are independent for adults in the state; H_a: they are not independent

parts.sample:
H_0: There is no association between days of exercise per week and sleep quality for adults in the state.
H_a: There is an association between days of exercise per week and sleep quality for adults in the state.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate test and calculate the expected count of adults who do not exercise and report poor sleep, showing your work.

rubric.point: Names a chi-square test for independence.
Expected count = (150)(127)/500 = 38.1, with the row total, column total and grand total shown.

parts.sample:
A chi-square test for independence, because one random sample of adults was classified by two categorical variables.
Expected (none, poor) = (row total)(column total)/(grand total) = 150*127/500 = 38.1.

parts.label: c

rubric.point: Random and 10%: the problem says a random sample of 500 adults, and 500 is less than 10% of the adults in a large state.
accept: both the random sample and the 10% condition stated in context

rubric.point: Large counts: every expected count is at least 5 (the smallest is 38.1).
accept: states all expected counts are at least 5, with the smallest or a list

parts.sample:
Random: a random sample of 500 adults.
10%: 500 is less than 10% of all adults in a large state.
Large counts: the expected counts are 38.1, 57.0, 54.9, 45.7, 68.4, 65.9, 43.2, 64.6, 62.2; every one is at least 5 (the smallest is 38.1).

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Calculate the chi-square statistic, the degrees of freedom and the p-value.

rubric.point: Chi-square statistic about 17.32, with the form sum of (O - E)^2/E shown or at least one component written out.
accept: chi^2 = 17.32 from technology with the formula named

rubric.point: Degrees of freedom (3 - 1)(3 - 1) = 4 and a p-value of about 0.0017 (between 0.001 and 0.0025 from Table C).
accept: df = 4 with a p-value of 0.0017 or 0.002

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: State the conclusion of the test at the significance level 0.05, in context.

rubric.point: Compares the p-value with 0.05 and makes the correct decision: because 0.0017 < 0.05, reject H_0.
accept: "since the p-value is less than alpha = 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis"

rubric.point: Conclusion in context with evidence language: there is convincing evidence of an association between days of exercise and sleep quality for adults in the state.
accept: convincing evidence that exercise and sleep quality are associated for adults in the state; no "proves" or causal claim

parts.sample: Because the p-value of 0.0017 is less than 0.05, we reject H_0. There is convincing evidence of an association between days of exercise per week and sleep quality for adults in the state.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Describe the association, using the cells that contribute most to the chi-square statistic.

rubric.point: Names cells with large components and their direction: more adults who do not exercise report poor sleep than expected (and fewer report good sleep), while adults who exercise 3 or more days report good sleep more often and poor sleep less often than expected.
accept: uses at least two of the four largest components (about 5.07, 4.04, 4.02, 4.00) with the direction of each

parts.sample: The largest components are none/poor (5.07: 52 observed against 38.1 expected), none/good (4.04: 40 against 54.9), 3 or more days/poor (4.02: 30 against 43.18) and 3 or more days/good (4.00: 78 against 62.22). Adults who do not exercise report poor sleep more often and good sleep less often than expected, and adults who exercise 3 or more days a week report good sleep more often and poor sleep less often. Because this is an observational study, the data do not show that exercise causes better sleep.
